scope: Retain the email challenge deadline independently of the provider flow, reject expired code before unlock, preserve resend, and display Google flow errors in the existing auth menu notice.
commands: SEAMS_INTENDED_PRODUCTION=1 SEAMS_INTENDED_SKIP_BUILD=1 node tests/scripts/run-wallet-intended-isolated.mjs --require-google-token -- e2e/intended-behaviours/email-otp.unlock.contract.test.ts --grep 'Email OTP registration and unlock lifecycle'
findings: Production flow discarded challenge expiry; it now requires and checks the exact challenge deadline.
Production Google login and registration errors were stored but omitted by the menu notice; the existing notice now renders them.
The production route deliberately reuses an active challenge. This test shortens only the first browser-visible deadline; resend restores the valid server deadline.
The hosted OTP input submits automatically on the sixth digit. The scenario follows that behavior without a second submit action.
limits: The custom auth.unlockWithEmailCode API and removal of specialized public unlock methods remain open.
Pending Email OTP activation continuation and concurrent submit/cancel acceptance remain open.
This scenario verifies expiry rejection after challenge creation; malformed expiry inputs are rejected by the boundary parser but not separately exercised here.
